title: Update on COVID-19 Situation and Measures Given Emergence of New Variants
what_it_is: Update on COVID-19 Situation and Measures Given Emergence of New Variants

sections.label: COVID-19 reinfection, boosters, clinic capacity
sections.summary: Questions ask whether reinfections are rising, whether second booster eligibility will expand, and how primary care and telemedicine cope with patient spikes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry is observing an increasing trend in the COVID-19 reinfection rate given the continued emergence of new Omicron sub-variants; and (b) whether there are any plans to further expand the eligibility for second booster shots for younger age groups, especially when the vaccines are updated to deal with new variants or subvariants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health in view of the current wave of COVID-19 infections (a) what measures are in place or planned to be put in place to cope with the spike in the number of patients at general practitioner clinics, polyclinics and hospitals’ emergency departments; and (b) whether there are plans to further support the growth of the telemedicine sector in Singapore to provide medical services for mild cases and to reduce the number of infected persons visiting physical clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the recent wave of COVID-19 infections has resulted in much longer waiting times for patients at polyclinics and neighbourhood general practitioner clinics; (b) whether the waiting time and services can be improved; and (c) whether the capacity for primary care at the heartlands can be further stepped up.

sections.label: Foreign patients and COVID-19 bed capacity
sections.summary: Questions ask the number of foreign patient arrivals, utilisation of hospital capacity by foreign patients, and beds used and set aside for COVID-19 hospitalisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what is the number of foreign patient arrivals in Singapore in (i) 2022 year-to-date and (ii) each of the last five years; (b) what are the current utilisation rates of existing capacity by foreign patients in private and public hospitals respectively; and (c) what is the bed capacity in private and public hospitals (i) currently used and (ii) set aside, for COVID-19 hospitalisations in light of the rising number of COVID-19 cases.

sections.label: Falling infection numbers
sections.summary: Over the last 10 days infection numbers have been falling and the week-on-week ratio dipped below 0.9 over the last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Over the last 10 days, infection numbers have been falling and the week-on-week ratio has dipped below 0.9 over the last week.

sections.label: COVID-19 hospital bed capacity
sections.summary: Based on a worst-case projection for the current wave, plans are to set aside up to about 1,000 COVID-19 hospital beds for COVID-19 patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The first important measure to achieve that is to set aside sufficient bed capacity to cater to COVID-19 patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, in response to Mr Louis Chua, based on our worst-case scenario projection for the current wave, we have plans to set aside up to about 1,000 COVID-19 hospital beds for COVID-19 patients.

sections.label: Transfers and reduced hospital workload
sections.summary: For this infection wave, more transfers were made than the last, and hospitals cut business-as-usual workload by about 5%, mostly elective surgeries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As a result, for this infection wave, we have been able to make many more transfers than the last and this has made a significant difference to the workload of hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They have cut down on "business-as-usual" workload, by about 5% and this comprises of mostly elective surgeries.

sections.label: Infection prevalence and population protection
sections.summary: About 60% of local residents are estimated to have been infected; population protection against severe illness is achievable through vaccinations, and 2.4% of infected persons needed hospitalisation in the last Omicron wave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: From these samples, we estimate about 60% of local residents are likely to have been infected with COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: By and large, scientists around the world do not think herd immunity is achievable because the virus will continue to mutate, escape the protection of vaccines and then, infect people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What is achievable is population protection against severe illness through vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: During the last Omicron wave at the beginning of this year, 2.4% of infected persons needed hospitalisation.

sections.label: Seniors without booster shots
sections.summary: Vaccination now requires three doses, but 40,000 eligible seniors aged 60 and above have not received booster shots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is no longer a two-dose vaccination; it is three doses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, we have more or less hit a plateau – there remains 40,000 seniors, aged 60 and above, who have not received their booster shots, even though they are eligible.

sections.label: Second booster for 80 and above
sections.summary: Ten months of data show three mRNA doses still strongly prevent severe illness, so those 80 and above are recommended a second booster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And that is 10 months' worth of data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, our empirical data shows that after 10 months, the protective effect of three doses of mRNA vaccines remains very strong in preventing severe illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why as of now, our recommendation is for those who are 80 and above to receive their second booster, or fourth shot, to better protect against severe illness.

sections.label: Reporting infection episodes
sections.summary: With more reinfections, reporting will count infection episodes instead of infected persons from today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With more reinfections, from today, we will report the infection episodes instead of infected persons.

sections.label: Spending on respiratory infection scheme
sections.summary: By end FY2021 the Government spent about $178 million on over 11 million attendances at clinics for acute respiratory infections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As at end FY2021, the Government has spent about $178 million on the scheme for over 11 million attendances at private clinics and polyclinics for the treatment of acute respiratory infections.

sections.label: Waning protection and rising cases
sections.summary: As vaccine and prior infection protection wanes, the virus will circulate and cases rise, so vaccinations must be kept up to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As the protection of vaccines and prior infection wanes, the virus will circulate in our society again and cases will rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We must anticipate when that will happen and take the necessary precautions, including the most important of all, which is to keep our vaccinations up to date.

sections.label: Jab at suitable interval
sections.summary: Instead, a jab must be received at a suitable interval, maybe nine months or a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Instead, we must ensure that we get a jab at a suitable interval – maybe nine months or a year.

sections.label: Social restrictions for variant
sections.summary: If such a variant is encountered, social restrictions will become necessary again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If we encounter such a variant, I am afraid social restrictions will become necessary again.

sections.label: Booster doses for children
sections.summary: A third mRNA dose may be necessary for children aged five to 11, and MOH is preparing to roll out boosters in about two months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For children aged five to 11, a third mRNA dose may be necessary at some point to keep protection levels high and MOH is making the necessary preparations to roll out vaccination booster doses for this age group in about two months’ time.

sections.label: Vaccination for under-fives
sections.summary: MOH is preparing to start vaccination for those under five towards the fourth quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: MOH is preparing to start vaccination for those under five towards the fourth quarter of this year.

sections.label: Foreign patients in hospitals
sections.summary: Between 2017 and 2019, public and private hospitals saw about 32,000 foreign patients annually, about 3% of inpatients and day surgery patients.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Between 2017 and 2019, our public and private hospitals saw about 32,000 foreign patients annually, or about 3% of all inpatients and day surgery patients.

sections.label: Singapore's smoother BA.5 wave
sections.summary: High vaccination and booster rates and a recent BA.2 wave gave better protection against BA.5, so Singapore waded through the current wave more smoothly than Portugal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: In our case, due to a combination of factors – high vaccination rate, high booster rates and the fact that we recently went through a BA.2 wave which gives better protective effects against BA.5 – we have waded through this current wave much more smoothly, compared to Portugal.

sections.label: Subsidy schemes after Flu Scheme
sections.summary: Despite deactivation of the Flu Subsidy Scheme, current subsidy schemes, especially CHAS and polyclinic subsidies, continue to be there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Notwithstanding deactivation of the Flu Subsidy Scheme, as I have mentioned, the current subsidy schemes, especially CHAS, polyclinic subsidies, continue to be there.

sections.label: COVID-19 subsidies winding back
sections.summary: As Singapore lives with COVID-19, subsidies return to pre-COVID-19 schemes, while hospitalisation and testing stay fully subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As we enter into a phase where we are more prepared and better able to live with COVID-19, just as we wound back our SMMs, we also need to go back to the subsidies schemes, pre-COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Hospitalisation, testing – all these continue to be fully subsidised.

sections.label: Mobile vaccinations for non-seniors
sections.summary: Mobile vaccinations for those who are not seniors will be done and have been done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for mobile vaccinations, for those who are not seniors, we will do so and we have been doing so.

sections.label: No herd immunity at 100%
sections.summary: Even at 100% vaccination, Singapore will not have herd immunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I am sorry to disappoint Mr Seah Kian Peng.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But even if we hit 100%, we will not have "herd immunity".

sections.label: Mobile and home vaccination coverage
sections.summary: Mobile and home vaccination teams have been useful, and Singapore has 93% vaccination coverage and 79% booster coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mobile teams have been useful; home vaccination teams have been useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But on the other hand, compared to other countries, we are 93% covered by vaccinations; 79% covered by booster.

sections.label: Rules do not provide for it
sections.summary: Current rules do not provide for that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Currently, our rules do not provide for that.

sections.label: 1,000 beds public hospitals
sections.summary: The 1,000 beds mentioned referred to public hospitals only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The 1,000 beds I mentioned referred to public hospitals only.
